title: Forgotten Time Capsule Found After 50 Years
paragraphs: A time capsule buried by schoolchildren in 1976 to mark their school’s fiftieth birthday has been dug up by builders at Hollowmere Primary School, half a century after it was placed in the ground. The discovery has brought back happy memories for the former pupils who filled it – and delighted the children who attend the school today.

The builders were digging the foundations for a new outdoor classroom last Tuesday when a spade struck something hard. “At first, we thought it was an old pipe,” said builder Dan Walsh. “Then we scraped away the mud and saw the words ‘DO NOT OPEN UNTIL 2001’ painted on the lid. We downed tools straight away and fetched the head teacher.”

Head teacher Mrs Helen Carter could hardly believe her eyes. “There have always been stories about a time capsule, but nobody knew where it was,” she explained. “The teacher who organised it retired long ago, and the tree that marked the spot was cut down when our school hall was built. In the end, everyone simply forgot about it.”

Mrs Carter decided that the capsule should not be opened until the people who had filled it could be there. She placed an appeal in the local newspaper and on the school’s website. Within a fortnight, more than thirty former pupils had been in touch, including one who now lives in Canada.

On Friday afternoon, the rusty metal box was finally opened in front of a packed school hall. Inside, wrapped in plastic bags, were letters written by the pupils, a class photograph, a school tie, a cassette tape of the school choir and a newspaper from the day the capsule was buried. Some of the letters had been damaged by damp, but most could still be read.

One letter belonged to Margaret Price, who was ten years old when she wrote it and is now sixty. She was invited to read it aloud. The audience roared with laughter when she reached her prediction that, by 2001, everyone would fly to school by jetpack, and Mrs Price giggled so much that she could hardly finish the sentence. However, her voice wobbled when she read the final line: “My gran helped me to write this letter.” Afterwards, she explained that her grandmother had died many years ago. “Seeing those words again made me feel as if she was right there beside me,” she said quietly.

The discovery has fascinated the school’s current pupils. Amira Hassan, aged 11, said: “It’s strange to think that the grown-ups were once our age. It made me wonder what people will think of us in fifty years’ time.”

The school now plans to bury a new time capsule this summer to celebrate its 100th birthday. This time, nothing will be left to chance: the exact spot will be marked on a map, and copies of the map will be kept at the school, the town museum and the local library. The new capsule will be opened in 2076.

questions.prompt:
Look at paragraph 1.
Find and copy a group of words that means fifty years.
What did the builders first think the time capsule was?

Look at paragraph 2.
Why do you think the builders “downed tools straight away”? Tick one.
options: They were frightened that the box might explode.
They realised the box might be important to the school.
Their spade had broken.
It was time for their lunch break.

questions.prompt:
Look at paragraph 3.
Mrs Carter “could hardly believe her eyes”.
What does this phrase suggest about how she felt? Tick one.
options: unable to see properly
angry with the builders
bored
very surprised

questions.prompt:
Look at paragraph 4.
Within a **fortnight**, more than thirty former pupils had been in touch…
Which of these is closest in meaning to **fortnight**? Tick one.
options: two days
two months
two weeks
one night

questions.prompt: According to the text, why was the time capsule not opened as soon as it was found? Tick one.
options: Mrs Carter wanted the people who had filled it to be there.
The lid was rusted shut.
The builders were not allowed to touch it.
The words on the lid said it must not be opened until 2076.

questions.prompt: Using information from the text, decide whether each statement is true or false.
statements: The time capsule was buried to mark the school’s fiftieth birthday.
One of the former pupils now lives in Australia.
All of the letters had been ruined by damp.
The new time capsule will be opened in 2076.

questions.prompt:
Look at paragraph 6.
How do you think Margaret Price felt as she read her letter aloud? Give two different feelings, using evidence from the text to support each one.
questions.model: At first she felt amused, because she “giggled so much that she could hardly finish the sentence” when she read her prediction about jetpacks. Later she felt emotional and a little sad, because “her voice wobbled” when she read the line about her gran, who had died many years ago.
points: Amused or happy, with evidence, e.g. she giggled at her jetpack prediction
Sad, emotional or moved, with evidence, e.g. her voice wobbled when she read the line about her gran

questions.prompt:
Look at paragraph 8.
Why do you think the spot where the new capsule is buried will be marked on a map, with copies kept in three places? Tick one.
options: so that visitors can dig it up whenever they like
because the builders asked for a map
so that new pupils can find their way around the school
so that it is not forgotten like the first one

questions.prompt: Number these events from 1 to 5 to show the order in which they happened.
items: The box was opened in the school hall.
Mrs Carter placed an appeal in the local newspaper.
Builders dug up a rusty metal box.
Margaret Price read her letter aloud.

questions.prompt: Why does the report begin with a paragraph that sums up the whole story? Tick one.
options: to describe exactly what was inside the time capsule
to give the reader the most important facts straight away
to give the builder’s opinion of the time capsule
to explain how to make a time capsule

questions.prompt: Which of these is the best summary of the report? Tick one.
options: A builder found some old toys that a pupil had lost in 1976.
A school celebrated its 100th birthday by building a new school hall.
Builders found a school time capsule from 1976, and former pupils came back to see it opened.
Former pupils were angry that their time capsule had been lost for so long.
